tagline: Past the long green that ran a war, to the Shetucket.
intro: Route 207 leaves Route 85 in Hebron and runs sixteen miles east, between Williams and Brewster ponds, through the center of Lebanon and on through Franklin past Gages Pond, to end on the west bank of the Shetucket River at Baltic.

In the Revolution Lebanon was a base of American operations. Jonathan Trumbull, the only colonial governor to side with the Patriots, ran a Council of Safety here that met more than 1,100 times, mostly in his own house. The French horse of the duc de Lauzun wintered in town in 1780 and 1781, and Lauzun later wrote that only Siberia could give an idea of the place.

moments.title: Lebanon Green
moments.text: A mile of grassy common, a rare survivor from the 18th century and still partly farmed, with the 1730 War Office and the Trumbull houses facing it.

moments.title: Baltic
moments.text: The village grew up around a cotton mill on the Shetucket, and nearly all of it is a historic district now, though fire took most of what was left of the mill in 1999.
